purpose: Speculative Tangent Space interface proposals; no application implementation

assets.title: A home for each Tangent
assets.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a high-fidelity, premium product-design proposal board for the web application "Tangent Space". This is a concrete interface exploration, not a promotional landing page or a moodboard. Render flat straight-on screenshots, no device frames, no perspective, no floating UI. Landscape board, very high resolution, sharp readable typography. Use a 2 by 2 grid of FOUR equally sized desktop browser-viewport screenshots, with small tasteful numbered captions OUTSIDE each screenshot. Maximize space for the interfaces; no giant board title or explanation paragraphs.
Product model: Tangent Space hosts Tangents (communities); each Tangent has Topics (conversations); each Topic has Posts. Never call them rooms or channels. Humans and agents participate together. A small plain "Agent" label appears beside Lumen; no robot mascot.
Shared example content across all four screens: community named "Night Garden", purpose "Small observations, bigger questions." Its persistent identifying photograph shows a lush botanical conservatory at dusk, warm amber lights and deep green foliage. The identical recognizable conservatory photograph must recur on the community card, community header and small thread identity thumbnail. Two other communities are "The Workshop" (sunlit wood workbench photo) and "Far Horizons" (misty coastal headland photo).
Signed-in person is Mara. Current conversation is "What makes a city feel alive?" with opening post by Mara: "The places I return to always leave room for the unexpected. What does that look like in your city?" Replies: Ivo: "The corner bakery. Nobody hurries you." Lumen with small Agent badge: "A bench can matter as much as a landmark." Use only this concise readable content, not lorem ipsum. A public thread clearly says "Public · Anyone can read"; its composer clearly says "Public reply" with "Write a reply..." and a "Post reply" button. Place author names and reply relationships clearly.
All four screens share one consistent app navigation, typography, component language and community identity. Purposeful whitespace, realistic functional density, clear hierarchy and high contrast. No huge unused blank areas. No decorative dashboards, no charts, no unread-count pressure, no notification badges, no fake online statistics, no modals. Onboarding is installation-owner setup, not mandatory newcomer registration. Visitors can read public communities without a setup questionnaire.
Captions outside the four frames must read: "01 / Create your Tangent", "02 / Find your place", "03 / Inside Night Garden", "04 / Read and reply".

DIRECTION A: A HOME FOR EACH TANGENT. Place-first navigation. Make this warm, intimate, visually rich and calm. Deep midnight ink surfaces, warm ivory text, restrained moss and pale gold highlights; excellent readable contrast. Beautiful editorial serif only for large page titles, crisp humanist sans for all controls and body text. Photographs are vibrant but natural. Community images are meaningful wayfinding. This is a polished useful community product, not a streaming service, social metrics dashboard or generic SaaS template.
Frame 01: Owner setup. Compact top logo and horizontal progress "Account ✓  /  Data ✓  /  First Tangent". Balanced two-column layout: left form heading "Make a place for good conversations", field "Name" set to "Night Garden", field "What brings people here?" with the stated purpose, a clear image selection control; right live preview of the conservatory image community card. Beneath form a quiet summary "Data: SQLite · Saved on this server", primary "Create Night Garden". Show a real inviting product setup, not a technical wizard.
Frame 02: Returning person's Space landing. Header Tangent Space left; "Explore" and "Recent" navigation, search, Mara avatar right. Page title "Find your next good conversation". A compact horizontal "Recently visited" link to the city conversation, not a giant activity feed. Main visual is three generous image-led community cards in a clean three-column collection. Each card combines rich image, community name, a one-sentence purpose and ONE specific latest-conversation title below it. Night Garden card shows city conversation; Workshop shows "What are you making?"; Far Horizons shows "A place you would return to". Images are not covered with tiny white text. A modest "Create a Tangent" action.
Frame 03: Community home. Same header. Conservatory image becomes a shallow wide masthead, with clear "Night Garden" and purpose below or beside, small "About" and "Manage" links, "Start a conversation" primary action. The majority of viewport is a comfortable conversation list: city conversation with opening excerpt and three participant avatars, then "An ordinary thing worth noticing" and "A small ritual for the week". No grid of topics indistinguishable from community cards. A small welcome note occupies the right sidebar, titled "A good place to begin", with a short human welcome. Image is a landmark, not half the viewport.
Frame 04: Active Topic. Compact breadcrumb "Night Garden / Conversation" with a tiny matching photograph; serif city title and public audience line. Quiet narrow list of other conversations on left, wide readable central post column with Mara opening, Ivo reply, Lumen Agent reply, and public composer beneath. The community photograph recedes to thumbnail and subtle header color so reading dominates. Clear visible reply action on each post. Keep the thread plain and humane, no speech bubbles, no oversized card borders around every post. A restrained text control "Conversation settings". A subtle "2 new replies · Show" inline update affordance may sit above composer without disrupting reading. This is the same community as previous screens, unmistakably.

DIRECTION B: THE READING DESK. Activity-first navigation with a compact community shelf and a calm reading workspace. A genuinely different information architecture from image-card galleries: organize around what the person wants to read next. Warm off-white canvas, graphite text, deep teal primary controls, restrained mint selection background; modern high-legibility sans serif throughout, generous but efficient rhythm, thin dividers, soft corners. Quiet sophisticated productivity-meets-community feel, never email inbox chrome or a to-do app.
Frame 01: Owner setup. A minimal left journey rail "Account ✓", "Data ✓", "First Tangent" beside a warm centered creation form. Heading "Give your conversations a home". Night Garden name and purpose fields, photograph picker with a compact wide preview, quiet "SQLite · Saved on this server" data summary, "Create Night Garden" teal button. The same compact thumbnail identity style previews how the community will appear in the desk.
Frame 02: Space landing is a reading desk. Header Tangent Space, search, Mara. Page heading "A little time to catch up". A horizontal SHELF of three compact landscape community thumbnails with names Night Garden / The Workshop / Far Horizons. Below shelf, asymmetric two-column layout: broad "Recent conversations" with clean stacked preview rows, each row begins with a small community photo and shows conversation title, author and one-line excerpt; narrow "Replies to you" section with specific reply context, no counts or urgency colors. A clear "Explore Tangents" path remains visible. City conversation is selected pale mint. No giant image tiles here. This screen offers concrete reading choices, not an empty personalized dashboard.
Frame 03: Night Garden community home uses the same desk layout. Narrow left shelf/list of communities; main area has compact photograph-and-purpose community header, "Start a conversation" action, a full practical list of titled conversations with short excerpts and authors. Right area offers "About Night Garden" and a concise welcome. A recognizably complete place beyond the queue. The featured conservatory image is smaller than on a gallery but always recognizable.
Frame 04: Desktop split-view live conversation. Stable app header and thin community image shelf. Left 28% is a "Recent conversations" queue with small community photos, selected city row highlighted pale mint. Right 72% is a large white reading pane: small Night Garden image and name, prominent city title, "Public · Anyone can read", Mara opening, Ivo reply, Lumen Agent reply, public reply composer and teal Post reply button. Real readable text occupies the pane, not dozens of metadata icons. Small "Conversation settings" control near topic title. New replies have a quiet "2 new replies · Show" affordance that does not jump the scroll. The layout visibly preserves surrounding reading context while a conversation is open. Artwork works as compact navigation rather than page decoration.

DIRECTION C: THE COMMUNITY JOURNAL. Conversation-first, editorial navigation. A distinct, thoughtfully composed editorial reading product where each Tangent is a living community journal with a photographic cover. Warm paper ivory canvas, charcoal text, deep forest actions and small burnt-orange accents; restrained elegant serif headings and readable sans body text. Sophisticated literary/editorial warmth without fake paper textures, typewriter nostalgia, handwritten text, magazine ads or newspaper clutter. Human intimacy, generous reading measure, coherent layout.
Frame 01: Owner setup reads like creating the cover of a community journal. Simple top progression "Account ✓  /  Data ✓  /  First Tangent". Left column heading "A place for your shared curiosities", Night Garden name, purpose field, photograph selection and "Create Night Garden" forest button. Right column a tall beautiful cover preview: conservatory photo, Night Garden title and purpose set cleanly beneath it. Small "SQLite · Saved on this server" summary. This is still a usable web form, not a full-bleed illustration.
Frame 02: Landing page titled "Conversations worth settling into". Navigation Tangent Space, Explore, Recent, search, Mara. Three vertical editorial community covers in a carefully spaced collection. Each cover combines the community photograph, clear community name and purpose, then a prominent actual conversation headline and a short opening excerpt beneath. The Night Garden cover's conversation is the city question; Workshop shows "What are you making?"; Far Horizons shows "A place you would return to". A small "Recently visited" line at top names the city topic. Every image tells which community a conversation belongs to; no algorithmic infinity feed, no engagement scores. Cards feel like an invitation to read, not promotional event tiles.
Frame 03: Inside Night Garden, a shallow conservatory cover above name and purpose, "About" / "Manage" links and "Start a conversation". Main body is a journal of conversation previews in activity order: city headline, Mara author and a short full opening paragraph, "3 replies · Read conversation"; two smaller previews below "An ordinary thing worth noticing" and "A small ritual for the week". Thin horizontal rules, graceful serif topic headings. Narrow side area introduces the community with one short welcome. This is an overview of discussions, not one long undifferentiated post feed.
Frame 04: Topic as a readable article becoming a live conversation. Compact Night Garden photo signature, breadcrumb, large elegant city title, public audience label. One centered approximately 70-character reading column, Mara byline and opening paragraph, then a clear understated "The conversation" divider and Ivo / Lumen Agent replies with visible Reply controls. Public composer follows in the same column, forest "Post reply" button. Right quiet rail contains "In Night Garden" and two related conversation titles, plus Conversation settings. No enormous hero photograph in the reading view. Deep links and authors are obvious. A subtle "2 new replies · Show" update control above replies. The whole screenshot prioritizes reading and thoughtful response over scanning metrics.
